newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM CEO SEES CONTINUED QUARTERLY UPTREND.
newsitem.headline: UPM CEO SEES CONTINUED QUARTERLY UPTREND.

text.p: Europe's largest forest industry group UPM-Kymmene expects continued quarterly profit improvement, CEO Juha Niemela told Reuters Financial Television in an interview due to be broadcast on Thursday.

"What is important is that this last quarter was clearly better than the quarter before, so we have already had three consecutive quarters towards the better, and we expect that to continue," Niemela said.
UPM earlier said H1 profit after financial items rose 70 percent to 3.51 billion markka from 2.08 billion, including over two billion in gains from disposals booked at operating level.
Niemela said earnings from actual operations fell.
"Last year we had 11.3 (million markka) and now this year 8.8 (million markka)," Niemela said.
Asked if he shared the view that the forestry sector was improving, he said: "It is a gradual way upwards, not the kind that we saw two-three years ago."
Pulp prices are improving partly on strikes in Canada but mainly on strong demand, and paper prices were rising "not quickly but slightly", he said.

Niemela repeated that UPM has a strategy to become a considerable player especially in magazine papers in U.S. markets, but he declined any comment on whether UPM was now involved in any acquisition talks.
